hints: Think about what volatile really means, how easily a liquid turns into a gas and escapes.
Recall what you see in the lab, chlorine is a gas at room temperature while bromine is a liquid, so chlorine must escape more easily.

walkthrough:
**Recall what volatility means**

Volatility tells us how easily particles escape from the liquid to form a gas. A more volatile substance has a lower boiling point because its particles need less energy to separate.

Think: gas at room temp > liquid at room temp for volatility.

**Compare chlorine and bromine**

Both exist as simple diatomic molecules, $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$, held together by London dispersion forces between molecules. Chlorine is a gas at room temperature, bromine is a liquid, so chlorine escapes much more easily.

So: more volatile = chlorine.

**Explain with intermolecular forces**

London dispersion forces get stronger with more electrons and a larger electron cloud. Bromine has many more electrons (35 per atom) than chlorine (17 per atom), so its temporary dipoles are stronger.
$$\text{strength of London forces: } \text{Br}_2 > \text{Cl}_2$$
Stronger forces in bromine mean more energy is needed to separate $\text{Br}_2$ molecules, so bromine is less volatile.

options.A: Incorrect. The explanation part is right that forces are greater in bromine, but the identity is wrong. Stronger forces hold bromine molecules together more tightly, making bromine less volatile, not more.
options.B: Incorrect on both parts. Bromine is not more volatile than chlorine, and forces are not greater in chlorine. Bromine has more electrons so its London dispersion forces are stronger than those in chlorine.
options.C: Correct. Chlorine is the more volatile element because it is a gas at room temperature while bromine is a liquid. This is because London dispersion forces are stronger in $\text{Br}_2$ due to more electrons, so $\text{Br}_2$ needs more energy to separate and evaporate.
options.D: Incorrect explanation. Chlorine is indeed more volatile, but not because its forces are stronger. If its forces were stronger it would be less volatile. In fact forces are weaker in chlorine than in bromine.
